title: Mitigating LLM Hallucinations: Instruction Fine-Tuning, RAG & Citation Grounding
summary: Drawing from curating Gemini instruction fine-tuning workflows at Innodata and building FAISS RAG pipelines, here is a two-pronged defense against model fabrication.
architecture_flow: Query -> Dense Embedding -> FAISS Top-K (Score >= Threshold) -> Strict Citation Prompt -> Grounded Answer

sections.heading: High-Signal Instruction Tuning & Safety Audits
sections.body: Curating adversarial edge cases and teaching models when to abstain ('insufficient context') drastically reduces unsupported claims during post-training.

sections.heading: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Similarity Gates
sections.body: By chunking verified documents with overlap, indexing dense embeddings in FAISS, and enforcing minimum cosine similarity thresholds plus mandatory [doc_id | chunk] citations, every claim remains auditable.

takeaway: Combining post-training alignment with retrieval similarity gates transforms LLMs from creative text generators into verifiable enterprise knowledge engines.

title: From Symbolic Rules to Agentic Workflows: Designing Reliable AI Systems
summary: Modern AI has evolved from static prediction endpoints into multi-step reasoning agents. Enterprise deployments succeed when probabilistic models are wrapped in deterministic verification gates.
architecture_flow: User Intent -> Input Guardrails -> Reasoning / Tool Execution -> Verifier Gate -> Action or HITL

sections.heading: Deterministic Guardrails
sections.body: Wrap stochastic model outputs with strict schema validation, input sanitization, and confidence thresholds before executing downstream actions.

sections.heading: Atomic Reasoning Trace Verification
sections.body: Auditing intermediate reasoning steps catches subtle logical fallacies even when a model stumbles onto a plausible-looking answer.

takeaway: Production AI reliability is an engineering systems problem—combining mathematical bounds, deterministic verification, and continuous evaluation.

title: The Mathematics of Generalization: Regularization, Bias-Variance & Hyperparameter Tuning
summary: How L1/L2 regularization, stratified k-fold cross-validation, and margin maximization pushed our Fake News NLP pipeline to 95.0% out-of-sample accuracy.
architecture_flow: min_w [ (1/N) Sum L(y_i, w^T x_i) + L1||w||_1 + L2||w||_2^2 ] -> 95.0% Out-of-Sample Accuracy

sections.heading: L1 vs. L2 Regularization in High-Dimensional Text
sections.body: Adding penalty terms constrains parameter norms, preventing high-dimensional TF-IDF n-gram features from memorizing rare noise tokens.

sections.heading: Stratified K-Fold Validation
sections.body: Preserves class proportions across every validation fold, eliminating optimistic data leakage during GridSearchCV.

takeaway: Strong feature engineering paired with regularized linear models and stratified validation often delivers superior speed and interpretability.

title: Why 80% of Data Science Impact Happens Before Model.fit()
summary: Lessons from scaling unstructured speech and text pipelines by 6,000x at Swecha: schema enforcement, deduplication, and metric alignment beat complex architectures.
architecture_flow: Raw Unstructured Logs -> Unicode & Regex Normalization -> Deduplication -> Feature Store -> Model

sections.heading: Distribution & Drift Auditing
sections.body: Check missingness mechanisms (MCAR vs. MAR), heavy-tailed outliers, and covariate shift between historical and live windows.

sections.heading: Metric Alignment with Operational Risk
sections.body: Choose asymmetric loss metrics (Precision-Recall AUC or MAPE) when false positives and false negatives carry vastly different business costs.

takeaway: A simple model trained on clean, de-duplicated, domain-aligned data will consistently outperform a complex model trained on noisy pipelines.

title: Why SARIMA Outperformed ARIMA by 60% RMSE on 15-Year Energy Demand
summary: Using Augmented Dickey-Fuller stationarity testing and seasonal differencing (D=1, s=12) to cut forecasting RMSE from 412.8 MWh down to 164.7 MWh.
architecture_flow: Observed Series Y_t = Trend (T_t) + Seasonality (S_t) + Residual Noise (E_t)

sections.heading: Seasonal Decomposition & Stationarity
sections.body: Power consumption exhibits strong 12-month seasonal cycles alongside long-term economic drift that non-seasonal ARIMA smooths over.

sections.heading: Window Functions & Anomaly Baselines
sections.body: Combining STL decomposition with rolling SQL window baselines isolates true demand spikes from predictable seasonal peaks.

takeaway: Effective analytics isolates the specific structural driver decision-makers need to act on.
